scenario_results.observed: Re-run at the follow-up commit. PaymentReconciliationIntegrationTest on PostgreSQL: the kitchen's NOT_RECEIVED report moves the deposit to DISPUTED and, in the same transaction, opens exactly one support case PAYMENT/HIGH/OPEN for the order; a retry with the stale payment version is refused (409/422) and still leaves one case. The case description contains no transfer reference, recipient account or amount. The order's own customer sees the PAYMENT case in GET /api/v1/support/cases; another customer's list does not contain it; support staff see it in /api/v1/ops/cases. Recipient approval, queue authorization and the 'no staff RECEIVED' rules from run 20261013-MB-052 stay covered by the same suite.

Re-run at the follow-up commit. After the dispute, the cook rejects the order (RECONCILE_PENDING) and finance (recent MFA) records REFUND_OWED with a reason: the order still has exactly one open PAYMENT case (partial unique index support_case_open_payment_uq plus INSERT ... ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING). The refund flow to REFUNDED, the append-only timeline and the customer notifications (b8006db) are unchanged. Staff resolve the case by hand; it is not closed automatically.

findings: MB-052 follow-up (863edf0): automatic PAYMENT support case on DISPUTED, RECONCILE_PENDING and REFUND_OWED through the existing OrderCases port. Self-review, not independent review.

Authorization: the case belongs to the order's customer; customer list/detail stay owner-scoped; kitchens have no case API; staff access unchanged (support.case). Customers cannot open PAYMENT themselves (CUSTOMER_CATEGORIES unchanged).
Money: no amount, reference or account in the case; payment state machine, versioning and the ledger untouched. Live money remains blocked by D16 gates.
